title: Peperoni con Bagna Cauda
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Sweet roasted Piedmontese peppers served warm and generously bathed in bagna cauda, the region's classic garlic and anchovy sauce, a simpler standalone twist on the communal original.
longDesc: While bagna cauda is traditionally a shared dipping experience for a whole table of raw and cooked vegetables, this version roasts sweet peppers specifically and dresses them directly with the sauce, letting the peppers' natural sweetness play against the pungent garlic and anchovy.
ingredients: 150 ml (⅔ cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Roast the whole peppers at 220°C (425°F) for 25–30 minutes, turning occasionally, until the skins blister and blacken.
Transfer to a covered bowl to steam for 10 minutes, then peel off the skins, remove the seeds, and slice into strips.
Meanwhile, combine the garlic and olive oil in a small saucepan and warm over very low heat for 15–20 minutes, until the garlic is completely soft and mellow, without browning.
Add the anchovy fillets and stir, letting them dissolve completely into the garlic-infused oil.
Stir in the butter until melted and smooth.
Arrange the roasted pepper strips on a plate and spoon the warm bagna cauda generously over them.
Finish with fresh parsley and serve warm.
chefTips: The garlic must cook low and slow until fully mellowed — any browning turns it bitter.
Roasting the peppers until the skins are properly blackened makes them much easier to peel.
This dish can be served warm or at room temperature, both work well.
commonMistakes: Cooking the garlic over heat that's too high, causing it to brown and turn bitter.
Not roasting the peppers long enough, making the skins difficult to remove cleanly.
Serving the sauce too cold, which mutes its aromatic qualities.
reheating: Reheat gently, taking care not to let the sauce boil.
healthBenefits: Bell peppers are an excellent source of vitamin C; anchovies provide omega-3 fatty acids.
culturalNote: This dish offers a simpler, standalone way to enjoy Piedmont's beloved bagna cauda sauce, pairing it directly with the region's naturally sweet roasted peppers.
